items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: for instance, Duke Ellington, whoever could get out a discography on him, keeps on coming.

ctx.x: That's Jorgen Grunet-Jepson. Jepson. He's done a lot of them. He did Armstrong, and he's very good. Oh, yeah. I don't think he's perfect. None of them are. But I think he's very good.

Well, Moses, I don't know how they do what they do. Years ago, I decided that those things were impossible tasks, not on Jelly Roll, because his is limited now. It has been for 20-odd years. But on these people that keep on, for instance, Duke Ellington, whoever could get out a discography on him, keeps on coming. And Blackstone in New Orleans, he went half crazy and had to quit, I think.
Yeah. But there's a lot of things that are on here. Well, what is the significance of the tune Mama Mita? Was that...?
